performers: National Symphony Orchestra of London, Stanford Robinson
intro: Stanford Robinson and the National Symphony Orchestra of London open the Waltz of the Flowers with the harp’s long flourish and the horns’ unhurried song. This is the first side of their 1945 Decca recording.

sections.label: Intro · Wind chords and harp cadenza
sections.mNote: The harp delays the dance with long runs of broken chords

sections.label: A · Horns begin the D-major waltz
sections.mNote: The horns sing above a three-beat string accompaniment

sections.label: B · Answering phrases above the strings
sections.mNote: Long melodies pass above bass notes and offbeat chords

sections.label: C · The waltz continues in D major
sections.mNote: The three-beat accompaniment carries the later phrases

cues.title: The harp holds the floor
cues.text: Woodwind and horn chords make way for the harp’s cadenza. Its broken chords range up and down before settling into a few held chords. Tchaikovsky marks the solo ad libitum, leaving the harpist room to linger.
cues.evidence: Jurgenson orchestral score, plate 17668, pp. 3–5, introduction and harp cadenza. https://urresearch.rochester.edu/fileDownloadForInstitutionalItem.action?itemId=22387&itemFileId=71624
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Horns above the dance
cues.text: The horns introduce the D-major waltz, marked dolce cantabile. Plucked bass notes and two answering string chords mark out each bar. A solo clarinet answers the horns with a curling phrase.
cues.evidence: Jurgenson score, plate 17668, pp. 5–6: horn theme, string accompaniment and solo clarinet replies. https://urresearch.rochester.edu/fileDownloadForInstitutionalItem.action?itemId=22387&itemFileId=71624
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: January at Kingsway Hall
cues.text: Robinson and the orchestra record this side at Kingsway Hall in January 1945, with the war in Europe not yet over. Decca issues the record in September, with the waltz spread across two sides.
cues.evidence: Commons gives 18 January 1945 (Decca K1144, matrix AR9079-2, released September 1945): https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:PDP-CH_-_National_Symphony_Orchestra_of_London_-_Stanford_Robinson,_conductor_-_The_Nutcracker_Suite,_Op._71_-_Waltz_of_the_Flowers_-_Tchaikovsky_-_Decca-k1144-ar9079.flac ; Damian’s 78s gives 26 January 1945 for matrices AR 9079-2 and 9080-2: https://music.damians78s.co.uk/2014/12/24/stanford-robinsons-nutcracker-and-bransby-williamss-scrooge/

cues.title: The suite succeeds first
cues.text: Tchaikovsky conducts the suite in Saint Petersburg on 19 March 1892. The ballet is still nine months from its première, but this waltz already has an audience. Two days later he tells Pyotr Jurgenson: “The suite from the ballet was successful.”
cues.evidence: Suite première 7/19 March 1892; Tchaikovsky to Pyotr Jurgenson, letter 4641, 9/21 March 1892. https://en.tchaikovsky-research.net/pages/The_Nutcracker_(suite)

composer.epithet: He could make a ballroom glitter, then let one unguarded melody tell us who was unhappy there.
facts: School of Jurisprudence; Saint Petersburg Conservatory, 1862–65, with Anton Rubinstein and Nikolai Zaremba
Nadezhda von Meck: an allowance, 1877–90, and a friendship conducted by letter
Three ballets; Eugene Onegin, The Queen of Spades and other operas
composer.background:
At Kamenka on 6 July 1878, Tchaikovsky was explaining to Nadezhda von Meck how he composed. Ideas arrived in the middle of conversations; he held them in his head until he could sketch them on the first sheet of paper that came to hand. Waiting for the right mood was no way to work. “Inspiration is a guest who does not like to visit the idle,” he told her. Then he broke off for dinner. At two o’clock he resumed, moving on to sketching, orchestration, fair copies and how far a symphony must keep to its traditional form. Here is the composer of extravagant passions in his own voice: observant, companionable, exact about his trade.

He was born in Votkinsk, where his father managed an ironworks. He grew deeply attached to his French governess, Fanny Dürbach, and began piano lessons at the end of 1845. The profession chosen for him was the law. In 1850 he entered the preparatory class of the Imperial School of Jurisprudence in Saint Petersburg. Four years later his mother died of cholera. He graduated in 1859 and took a post at the Ministry of Justice, while opera and concerts increasingly claimed his attention.
